Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC pattern notes: paired edge bars and ray fills

Observed solved instance `task-2d96d5f6` (correct after one wrong attempt; five demos requested). Save this pattern for future recurring tasks.

## Likely transformation
- Identify the background and two equal-length solid bars of the same color on opposite sides of the canvas (bars can be horizontal at top/bottom or vertical at left/right).
- Each bar serves as a directional source: extend the bar’s color into the canvas perpendicular to its edge, across the corresponding edge-coordinate interval. Sparse pixels of another color encode ray endpoints/marks. Extend that marker color in a straight line from its edge/bar toward the marker, recolor the marker itself to 4, and mirror/copy the active bar-coordinate positions to the opposing side as full-width fills. Preserve untouched cells and original bars.
- Exact orientation and which boundary intervals are active depend on the sparse marker pattern; infer by mapping the bar spans and marker coordinates. Demos below establish behavior in horizontal and vertical orientations.

## Concrete solved test rule
Grid was 21x27, background 8. Color-9 bars: left edge at column 0, rows 4–11; right edge at column 26, rows 13–20. These are two bars of length 8. Color-3 markers: (r4,c17), (r6,c21), (r7,c2), (r9,c22), (r10,c5), (r11,c17), 0-based.

Correct output:
- Preserve bars (9s).
- For each marker on rows 4,6,7,9,10,11, fill color 3 from c=1 up to c=marker_col-1, then replace marker cell with 4. The remaining cells stay 8. (For c2 marker on r7, only c1 gets 3.)
- Copy active row pattern onto opposite bar rows by offset +9: rows 13,15,16,18,19,20 are filled color 3 across c1..25; rows 14 and 17 stay 8 (apart from right edge bar). This corresponds to marker-bearing rows [4,6,7,9,10,11] shifted by the difference between the two bar spans.

## Demo evidence (important patterns)
- Demo 2 (22x15, bg9): horizontal color-2 bars at top cols 0–2 and bottom cols 5–7. Extend top bar's corresponding stripe down all rows (color8); dots at (13,7), (17,5), (19,6) extend vertically down to bottom bar, recolored 4 at their original cells. In output, marker 8 runs from marker row through row20; each endpoint marker becomes4.
- Demo 4 (14x12, bg7): bars color8 at top cols9–11 and bottom cols6–8. Top-side marker-color2 projection fills cols9–11 downward; bottom-side dots at (1,6),(11,7),(11,8) extend downward to bottom bar and become4 at original dot positions. Bars retain color8.
- Demo 3 (24x15, bg2): horizontal color8 bars top c7–11 and bottom c0–4. Dots color6 at (6,11),(10,10),(11,9); extend upward from each dot to the top bar, with dot cells changed to4. Other bar-coordinate stripe projection fills columns 2–4 all the way through the interior.
- Demo 1 (18x24, bg3): top/bottom color1 bars c0–6 and c14–20. Marker 5 pixels near bottom bar encode positions, and output shows their upward rays to the bar with markers changed to4; corresponding bar stripe pattern is carried across the canvas.
- Demo 5 (26x21, bg6): top/bottom color0 bars at top c11–13 and bottom c18–20; color1 markers at (20,13),(21,12). Output extends marker-color vertical rays upward from the markers to the top region, changing marker cells to4; fills matching bar-aligned stripe positions.

## Caution from first wrong submission
Do not fill the entire grid or assume all rows/columns between bars are colored. Preserve background outside the encoded ray/stripe regions. The sparse marker rows/columns determine which rays/stripes are active; 4 is the marker replacement color. Carefully distinguish marker's fill direction (toward its bar/boundary) from the repeated bar-derived stripe pattern. When there's uncertainty, request demos rather than guessing broadly.

# Continual-ARC task family notes (task-a130a2b4)

Learned from 2 demonstrations and a solved test instance. Recurring ARC pattern: a uniform background with several solid, axis-aligned monochrome rectangles. Each rectangle may have sparse corrupted cells (including cells replaced by background), and unrelated singleton noise pixels/colors occur outside the rectangles. Output restores each rectangle as a solid rectangle in its original color, and resets all off-rectangle noise to the background color. Infer rectangle extents/color from visible majority/interior evidence; don't preserve stray markers. There may be multiple rectangle colors in a single grid.

Evidence:
- Demo 1: background 1; color-6 rectangles at rows 2–5 cols 3–7, rows 7–13 cols 1–6, rows 17–21 cols 2–5, and rows 24–26 cols 6–8 (0-based); sparse intrusions/holes were repaired and outside noise reset to 1.
- Demo 2: background 5; color-4 rectangles rows 2–3 cols 4–5 and rows 3–8 cols 11–14; color-2 rectangle rows 3–9 cols 25–27. Noise and damaged cells repaired; outside speckles reset to 5.
- Solved test: background 0; rectangle fields in colors 8 and 1 were reconstructed, including noisy/missing cells; external speckles discarded. Correct answer was accepted after several attempts.

Practical approach: identify candidate rectangular patches using repeated same-color cells, treat other colors/background within their bounding boxes as corruption if the patch is strongly supported, preserve every supported rectangle, and replace all isolated noise elsewhere with the dominant background. Don't assume there is only one foreground color.
